page: Microsoft Azure FX64mds_v2 is an x86_64 virtual server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The server is equipped with 1344.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per core, alongside 3780 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory throughput. The server achieves top-tier performance in large-block memory bandwidth for both read and write operations, as well as in PassMark database operations and static web serving throughput. Multi-core CPU performance and Redis SET operations are rated as strong, while single-core performance falls into the average category.

From a resource density perspective, the FX64mds_v2 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads due to its massive RAM allocation and fast memory bandwidth. However, the average single-core performance represents a tradeoff for workloads that cannot leverage parallel processing or the specialized AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets.

This server configuration is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and data-intensive processing tasks that require substantial local storage and high memory capacity.
